results.story: The Machines Will Work. The Debt Might Not.
results.headline: Refuted: the investment-grade spread ended the window five basis points wider than August's average.
body: The ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread read 0.85% on October 2, 2026, the end of the four weeks after Labor Day, against an average of 0.80% over August's 21 daily readings (FRED series BAMLC0A0CM). The difference is +0.05%, five basis points, outside the 3 basis point band the rule names, so the answer to the question is no: the market did not price the window tighter than August.

What the series does not show, the press did. On September 22 Reuters reported spreads on AI-related issuers near 115 basis points against 78 for the broader investment-grade market, Alphabet paying a large concession on its August sale, and Aon's $13.5 billion financing drawing $65 billion of orders with its 30-year tranche tightening 35 basis points. Concessions normalized away from the AI complex and stayed wide inside it. That split is evidence here, not the rule.

The Call of Part 03, bearish on the credit of the buildout, expected the spread to widen, so a refuted test on this question is the market agreeing with the Call. Version 1 of this specification, approved on October 9 for a test already past, named a source that covered half the rule and a figure no public series reports; its reading of October 8 stays below under Earlier readings.

evidence.label: ICE BofA US Corporate Index option-adjusted spread, average 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31

callUpdate.note: Conviction unchanged: a wider spread at the end of the window is what the Call expected of the credit stack.

history.headline: Inconclusive: no public figure covers the September concessions
body: The test asked whether investment-grade borrowers paid narrower new-issue concessions on the $50 billion to $60 billion of paper priced in the four weeks after Labor Day 2026, September 8 to October 2, than on August's deals. The specification names SIFMA's issuance statistics as the public source and the dealer figures cited in JunkBondInvestor's Credit Weekly for the concession reading.

No public statistic reports an average new-issue concession for the window, and the dealer figures are not published as a series. Under the specification's own ambiguity rule the test is inconclusive. The Call stands as written.

evidence.label: Average new-issue concession on investment-grade deals priced Sept. 8 to Oct. 2, 2026
evidence.value: No public figure; dealer estimates are not published as a series
